title: Lenovo’s revenue jumps 48% to a record $30.2bn, but it books a $640m loss
excerpt: ‘We are seeing this real demand every day,’ says CEO Yang Yuanqing, as Lenovo results show record sales and a $640m loss.
content_html:
Lenovo’s revenue rose 48% to a record $30.2bn in the quarter to September, the company reported on Thursday. Under Hong Kong accounting rules, it also swung to a $640m net loss. A year earlier it made a $340m profit.

Lenovo’s shares slid more than 5% after the results, Bloomberg reported. Analysts had expected a loss of $38m. The quarter also brought Lenovo’s first operating loss since 2017, Yuan Gao wrote for Bloomberg.

Lenovo chairman and CEO Yang Yuanqing told Bloomberg the AI momentum is strong and sustainable.

“We are seeing this real demand every day,” Yang said.

Where the loss came from

Lenovo’s own figures show an operating loss of $117m, against a $643m profit a year earlier. Bloomberg tied it to a $1.9bn non-cash fair value loss from revaluing warrants.

Lenovo’s adjusted net income, which strips out those warrant charges and other items, rose 166% to $1.4bn. The company counts that figure as profit attributable to shareholders outside Hong Kong’s accounting standards.

AI servers carry the quarter

AI-related revenue grew 79% and passed $10bn for the first time, 36% of the total. Lenovo counts PCs and phones with AI chips, GPU servers, and AI services in that figure.

The Infrastructure Solutions Group, which makes servers and data centre gear, had its best quarter ever. Revenue jumped 178% to $11.3bn, and operating profit topped $1bn for the first time. GPU server revenue more than tripled, and Lenovo put its pipeline at $80bn.

The devices business grew 15% to $17.4bn, and services rose 20% to $3.1bn. Lenovo says its share of the PC market reached 23.8%.

That growth came while global PC shipments fell 21.2% in the third quarter, according to Omdia. The soaring cost of memory is squeezing Lenovo’s margins, Bloomberg reported. Omdia has tied this year’s PC slump to the memory crunch.

A $100bn target

“We are confident in sustaining this strong momentum and reaching US$100 billion in annual revenue as early as this fiscal year,” Yang said.

The results came days after Nvidia’s quarterly results. Washington also moved this week to curb remote access to US AI chips for Chinese developers. Yang told Bloomberg the rule has “no significant impact to our business.”

Lenovo’s shares have fallen more than 50% from their September peak, according to Bloomberg. In May, Lenovo results for the fourth quarter sent them up 15%.
